summary: I added docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md, which closes the sort-on-read question. It names the rule, which was written by SL-042's design, not by the person. It lists the measurements harness by harness: three Core Release runs at 8.84-44.12 ms against the 250 ms budget; the SL-042 figures; SL-044's window figures plus this build's re-run of T-003; and a Debug run. It also covers what the decision does not settle (live refresh, the memory figures), what would reopen it, and the exact find/replace text submitted for the engine's Scan Store line. That edit is reported as **not applied**, because the build stage has no way to write the engine's record. I appended one dated pointer line to the SL-042 doc after the paragraph that ends at line 126; the rest of the file is byte-identical. Following SL-062's precedent, each case obligation is checked by tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1 -Case C-00x. The script only reads files and git objects, every case passes, and each case failed against a planted mutant. The 34 ScanStore/ArchitectureRules tests, the full default Core suite (381/381, Debug) and window case T-003 on the published exe all passed after the edit.

files.why: The decision record. It covers: the question; the rule and who wrote it (SL-042's design), with git and ledger timing; the measurements, each named by harness; Decision: closed; Not covered (live refresh, SL-044 84 ms vs 50; the memory figures); the reopen conditions and how each trip wire runs; the engine line's submitted find/replace, marked 'not applied'; and a table mapping each case to its check.

Adds a blank line and 'Closed in SL-068 (2026-09-28) on these measurements; see docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md.' after the m9 paragraph that ends at line 126. Only added lines: git diff --numstat reads 2 0.
One executable check per case obligation (C-001..C-008), in the style of tests/bugs/SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1. It reads only files and git objects and is outside dotnet test and FsAnalyser.slnx.

obligations.how: There is no write path: the engine's architecture record is not in this worktree and no tool I hold writes it. The decision doc says 'Status: **not applied** by SL-068's build (2026-09-28)' and labels its wording 'the text submitted for the edit, not a copy of the record'. No other file carries the new sentence, and no architecture-record file was added. Criterion 1 stays unknown. Checked by SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1 -Case C-001 (exit 0; fails when the status says applied).

The submitted edit is written as an exact find/replace, applied only when the find text occurs exactly once. -Case C-002 feeds in four inputs. On the Scan Store sentence as handed to this build, the edit gives the design's line. On an already-edited line, a reworded line and a doubled line, it applies nothing and reports the text it found. The replace text does not contain the find text, so the edit cannot double-apply. Exit 0; fails when the replace re-includes the clause.

At base 6566536, line 126 ends the m9 paragraph: line 127 is blank and line 128 is the next heading. The pointer went in as new lines 128-129, inside the m9 section. -Case C-003 asserts: numstat 2 0; lines 1-127 byte-identical; everything after is the old text two lines down; one line-ending style. Exit 0; fails when line 126 is altered.

The doc lists every read of three Release runs: the build check's two plus this build's 40.42…8.84. It states the range as their exact min/max, **8.84 to 44.12 ms**, and gives the 5.7x margin. It quotes the brief's 9-40 only as the brief's figure. The engine sentence says 9-44, the rounded range. SL-042's 35.9-40.2 and SL-044's 97.9/47.5/141.9/44.0 each sit in their own item, named by harness and cross-checked against their source docs, and no range merges two harnesses. Checked by -Case C-004, exit 0; fails when a read is changed to 47.17.

`git log -S` shows the rule (SL-042 doc line 45), the figures (line 88) and SL-042's design record all first arrived in the same commit, b5c2b62. The ledger dates design attempt 29 at 2026-09-25T17:23:45Z, before build attempt 1 at 23:47:34Z. The doc states both facts and does not claim git shows the rule first. -Case C-005 detects which state holds and checks that the doc matches it. Exit 0; fails when 'same commit' is removed.

The timing test carries no Trait and no Skip. The default filter (Network!=TEST-NET-1&Network!=SMB-LOOPBACK&Cloud!=CF-SYNC-ROOT) therefore keeps it. Nothing sets a default Configuration, so a default run is Debug; the doc says this and says only a Release run can reopen the question. Confirmed by a real run: the default suite (no filter, no -c) passed 381/381 in Debug with the timing test included (22.39-36.98 ms). -Case C-006 checks all of this, plus that T-003 asserts the 500 ms open. Exit 0; fails when 'Debug' or the T-003 wording is mutated.

The doc has a '## Not covered' section between Decision and reopen conditions. It names re-sorting during a live refresh, cites docs/design/SL-044-folder-tree.md:17-19 (median 84 ms against a 50 ms bar, UI gap 866 against 250), and says a stored order there must be maintained under concurrent scan writes. The Decision section limits itself to a completed store, and the submitted engine line says nothing about refresh. Checked by -Case C-007, exit 0; fails when the heading is renamed.

The slice touched only the two docs, this check script and .taad/slices/SL-068/. It changed nothing under src/, no existing test and not .taad/fitness.yaml. None of the 40 fitness `files` globs reaches either doc, and nothing in src, tests or eng names either doc except this script. The 34 ScanStore/ArchitectureRules tests (Release, 34/34), the timing test and the full default suite (381/381) pass after the edit. Checked by -Case C-008, exit 0; fails when a file is planted under src/. The design expected 'only docs/design paths' in the diff; the one test file added is recorded under deviations.

Owed to validate-slice, not to this build. What the build found: in git the rule was not written before the result. SL-042 doc line 45, the figures at line 88 and SL-042's design record all first arrived in b5c2b62. The ledger does date SL-042's design at 2026-09-25T17:23:45Z, 6 h before the build that measured it (23:47:34Z). The decision doc states both, and -Case C-005 checks that its wording matches git.

Owed to validate-slice, not to this build. What the build found: the trip wire keeps running unattended. ScanStoreRollupTimingTests has no Trait and no Skip, the default filter keeps it, and the default `eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests` ran it (381/381 passed, Debug, reads 22.39-36.98 ms). The default configuration is Debug, not Release, and the doc says so. The 500 ms cold open is checked by window case T-003 outside dotnet test (passed on the published exe).

deviations: Design case C-008 expects `git diff --stat` to show only docs/design paths and no test reading docs/design. That cannot hold together with O-003..O-010, which require a runnable test for each case. I built the smallest thing that satisfies both: one standalone check script, tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1, following SL-062's merged precedent (tests/bugs/SL-062-LedgerCases.ps1). It is outside dotnet test and the solution, and reads only files and git. src/, every existing test, the Core.Tests project and .taad/fitness.yaml are untouched, and no pre-existing test or fitness rule reads either doc.

The design says reopen condition 2 (a cold open reaching 500 ms) 'has no automated check' and is measured by hand via `--report`. That contradicts the code. Window case T-003 (tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:2561-2619) opens a 100,000-file folder five times in the published exe and fails any open at 500 ms or over. `--report` carries no open timing; the hook reads LastFolderSortMs. The doc says T-003 checks it, outside `dotnet test`. I ran T-003 and it passed.

The design's 'temporary index about 400 KB at 100,000 children' assumed 100,000 ints. ChildrenLargestFirst sorts a ChildRow[], and Unsafe.SizeOf<ChildRow> measured 24 bytes on .NET 10.0.12, so a read is 2,400,000 bytes. The doc quotes the measured figure. The engine sentence's fixed wording, 'sorts a temporary index per call', was kept as the design wrote it.

The design quoted 8.98-44.12 ms from the build check's two runs. The doc also lists this build's Release run, which read as low as 8.84, so the stated range is 8.84 to 44.12 ms. It still rounds to the design's 9-44, so the submitted engine sentence is unchanged.

The design's must-verify on pre-registration came out 'arrived together' in git: the rule, the figures and SL-042's design record all first appear in b5c2b62. The ledger nevertheless dates the design 6 h before the build. The doc says both rather than choosing one framing.

The design names the old clause as 'and the children of each folder sorted largest first' and wants the sentence to end 'and the rolled-up totals per folder.'. That needs the 'and' to move, so the submitted find text is 'the rolled-up totals per folder, and the children of each folder sorted largest first.' It occurs exactly once in the line as handed, and -Case C-002 shows the result equals the design's line.
not_built: The edit to the engine's Scan Store architecture line itself. The record is not in this worktree and the build stage has no tool that writes it. As the design's fallback requires, it is reported 'not applied', with no in-repo stand-in, and slice criterion 1 stays unknown. The exact find/replace is in the last section of docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md. It applies cleanly: the line as handed to this build contains the find text exactly once. This is not an administrator matter, so no session is declared; it needs whoever has access to the engine's record.
follow_ups: Someone with access to the engine's architecture record applies the submitted find/replace in docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md (section "The engine's Scan Store line: text submitted for the edit"). Separately, the engine could give build stages a write path to that record: SL-042 and SL-068 both hit this wall, and this slice exists only because of it.

The Scan Store line's memory figures (699 MiB peak, 572 MB store) predate the as-built store (652.1 MiB retained at 5M entries, docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md:81-84). They were left alone as the design required; a slice about memory should re-audit them.

This build's T-003 cold open at the default window was 221.9 ms, of which the sort was 51.0 ms and 'the rest' 162.5 ms. SL-044 recorded 97.9 ms with 37.3 ms for 'the rest'. That is one run on a shared machine and still under 500 ms, but the non-sort share doubled; it is worth a second measurement before anyone treats it as a trend.

The design's open questions are still with the person: whether validate accepts criterion 1 as unknown; a new SL-068 doc versus a section in SL-042's doc; appending the pointer versus editing lines 120-126; and no fitness rule for 'no stored order' in Core.

tests.note: Exit 0. Debug reads 36.44-47.00 ms, under 250 in Debug too; quoted in the doc as not evidence for the rule.
First run: exit 1, one check failed. It was a bug in the check, not the doc: C-004's '9-40' regex matched '35.9 to 40.2'. I fixed it with number boundaries and C-004 then passed (exit 0).
Final run after the doc edits: exit 0, 'every check held'. Run individually, C-001..C-008 each exit 0 (9/15/12/17/12/15/8/10 checks).

tests.command: mutation pass: for each case, plant one wrong shape (status 'applied', replace re-including the clause, SL-042 line 126 altered, a read changed to 47.17, 'same commit' removed, 'Debug' changed to 'Release' and the T-003 wording removed, 'Not covered' renamed, a file planted under src/), run that case, then restore the bytes in finally
tests.note: Every mutant made its case exit 1 with the expected FAIL line. All files were restored and git status is unchanged.
The full default suite: no filter, no -c, so Debug. Exit 0, 381/381 passed. The trx shows ScanStoreRollupTimingTests ran in it (Debug reads 22.39-36.98 ms), which is the evidence for C-006/O-002.

This runs the product as it ships. It published artifacts/publish/FsAnalyser.App.exe (gitignored), built 100,000 files on disk in 29.2 s, and opened the folder in the real window through the hook. Cold open 221.9 ms at the default window (sort 51.0, rows 7.4, rest 162.5) and 115.3 ms as tall as the work area (sort 43.8); all 10 opens under 500 ms, only a screenful of rows built, largest file first. PASSED, exit 0.
Returned 24, so 2,400,000 bytes per 100,000-child read. This corrects the design's 'about 400 KB'.
